summary: Reviewed IDEA000059, IDEA000073 and IDEA000124 with bounded registry cards, duplicate screens, route-check, the admitted f77r/f80v/f85r1 pilot excerpts, and targeted predecessor reports. No joint contrast is executable from this packet: the only admitted sheor example is outside an amount frame; the polarity candidate has no independently identified marker; and the complete-recipe ledger lacks calibrated initial/final inventories and a frozen historical instruction grammar. No meaning, selection, experiment, or registry decision was made.

items.title: Dry/moist whole pairs operate on a shared amount frame
items.source_example: Admitted f80v.36 reads `soin okain sheor ol shey daly olshedy olal shedy lchy` (the three reader variants retain the locus, with reader-specific marks elsewhere). This is a real sheor occurrence, but it has no independently coded amount head/value pair and contains no cheor comparator in the packet.
items.known: GDT760 already reports cheor and sheor in three exact amount contacts on three pages, with common s/or/ar and value-II/III contexts, while retaining water and wine as rivals and zero confirmed lexemes. GDT762 keeps the dry/moist forms as replaceable content/state candidates; its next route is a bounded content/medium discriminator.
items.genuinely_untested: The registered substitutional operator claim remains scientifically untested. GDT760's already admitted amount examples establish the relevant source capacity globally, but the present pilot excerpt has no matched pair. More importantly, an ordinary-noun/template rival can also preserve amount-head/value syntax, so syntax preservation alone is not a discriminator even with the full amount deck.
items.strongest_rival: Unrelated material nouns accepted by a recurring amount template; the apparent dry/moist contrast may be an analyst gloss rather than an operator slot.
items.differing_consequence: The current syntax prediction is shared by both models. A useful contrast would instead require a predeclared state-slot or attachment consequence in matched cheor/sheor contexts against ordinary nouns; no such differing observation is available in the admitted pages.
items.decision: Do not select or rerun in this batch. Missing capacity is previously reviewed rather than a new failure (GDT760/GDT762 explicitly defer the full cached-occurrence comparison).
items.smallest_next_action: Using the already admitted/cached amount examples, freeze exact cheor/sheor occurrences plus matched ordinary-noun controls and test a consequence beyond shared amount syntax (state-slot or attachment behavior), without importing an English dry/moist gloss.

items.title: A polarity marker negates the operation rather than its result
items.source_example: Admitted f80v.32 is `s olkain shol kair or arolkeedy olky qolkain shedy` in ZL3b, with the known IT/RF segmentation and RF product uncertainty. GDT944 treats `s` here as a local nominal-marker assumption, not an independently observed polarity marker; arol(keedy) and shedy are also hypothesis-bound operation/product values. The following f80v.33 does not add a marked failure case.
items.known: GDT944 already preserves two same-locus alternatives, formation versus separation, and explicitly finds no discriminator; RF leaves the first product group unresolved. GDT687 separates whole-form action/result roles, and GDT700 records one occurrence-bound action-output hypothesis, but neither identifies a polarity marker or establishes polarity scope.
items.genuinely_untested: The operation-scoped versus result-scoped attachment question is still untested. An exploratory test does not require a confirmed polarity/event annotation; it requires a fixed candidate marker set, scope model, and observable coding rule. Those are not fixed here, and the `s` assumption cannot be reused as polarity evidence.
items.strongest_rival: A result-scoped marker that preserves the operation while denying the result state; a structural/editorial packaging account remains a credible no-polarity rival.
items.differing_consequence: Operation scope leaves the input asserted but suppresses the operation; result scope preserves the operation but suppresses the result. The admitted f80v case does not distinguish these because marker status and event/result meanings are stipulated together.
items.decision: Do not select. The fixed marker/scope model and raw coding rule are absent; confirmed polarity/event annotation is not required for exploratory screening. This review adds no new manuscript finding.
items.smallest_next_action: Freeze a candidate marker set, operation/result scope models, and raw observable consequences independently of German glosses; then classify matched records, retaining unresolved and editorial cases as non-testable.

items.title: Complete recipe program with linear material registers and an independently fixed final inventory
items.source_example: The admitted complete run f80v.30-.37 contains f80v.32 `... arolkeedy ... qolkain shedy` followed by f80v.33 `qokeedy qoker olkain olshedy qokey qokeey tchcthy lom`. GDT944 records formation/separation as two same-locus readings, no independent product identity, and no written continuation binding. f85r1 supplies process-looking sequences but no inventory observations.
items.known: The proposal already states that no historical instruction grammar, calibrated quantity, independently bound operands, or independent final scene is fixed. GDT701's sole serial chain has a written intermediate product but no separately named final result; GDT446 separates identity from executable context; GDT893's word-bijection source reconstruction does not force execution identities. W16 explicitly reports no independent physical simulation and missing material-transfer relations.
items.genuinely_untested: The complete finite-register program and terminal inventory prediction have not been executed as a scientific test. That is a design-level untested proposal, not evidence that the admitted f80v sequence supports it.
items.strongest_rival: A local serial/record grammar in which adjacent actions share context or an editorial checkpoint, with no conservation, register lifetime, or terminal inventory commitment.
items.differing_consequence: The ledger model requires every operand and register transition to be accounted for, conserves fixed quantities, and predicts an independently observed final inventory. The local-record rival permits unresolved or independent actions and makes no terminal prediction. The packet supplies neither independently fixed inventory endpoint.
items.decision: Do not select or expand. The missing inputs are PREVIOUSLY_REVIEWED_NO_CHANGE; no new source admission or image access is permitted in this batch.
items.smallest_next_action: Only after independent historical-grammar, quantity-calibration, operand-binding, and initial/final-inventory gates are registered should a finite ledger test be considered; otherwise retain this card as RAW_UNSCREENED.

root_review_corrections: IDEA000059: GDT760 amount examples are already admitted globally; the packet limitation is the pilot excerpt. Amount-syntax preservation is shared by the operator and realistic ordinary-noun rival, so it cannot be presented as the discriminator.

IDEA000073: confirmed polarity/event annotations are not required for an exploratory joint hypothesis. The actual missing prerequisite is a fixed marker/scope model with distinct observable raw consequences.
IDEA000124: retain strict historical-grammar, calibration, operand-binding, and independent terminal-inventory gates for any confirmation test.
